items.q: A 35-year-old man presents with severe colicky flank pain radiating down into the scrotum. A 4 mm calculus is noted on CT. At which physiological constriction is the calculus most likely to impact?
o: Crossing over the common iliac artery
items.exp: The vesicoureteric junction (VUJ) is the narrowest site along the entire ureter as it passes obliquely through the muscular bladder wall, making it the most frequent impaction site for calculi.
r: Correct. The vesicoureteric junction is the narrowest anatomical site, frequently trapping migrating calculi.
Incorrect. PUJ is a constriction, but stones that pass it commonly impact at the VUJ.
Incorrect. Pelvic brim crossing is the second constriction site.
Incorrect. Mid-lumbar ureter has no anatomical constriction.
items.kp: The vesicoureteric junction is the narrowest site along the ureter and the most frequent location for calculus impaction.

items.q: In which anatomical zone of the prostate gland do approximately 75% of prostate adenocarcinomas arise?
items.exp: The peripheral zone forms approximately 70% of the volume of the prostate gland and accounts for 75% of prostatic adenocarcinomas, which are easily palpated on digital rectal examination.
r: Correct. Peripheral zone is the primary site of origin for prostatic adenocarcinoma.
Incorrect. Transition zone is where benign prostatic hyperplasia originates.
Incorrect. Central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts and rarely develops carcinoma.
Incorrect. Anterior fibromuscular stroma is non-glandular.
items.kp: Seventy-five percent of prostate adenocarcinomas originate in the peripheral zone, palpated via digital rectal exam.

items.q: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causing lower urinary tract obstructive symptoms predominantly arises from which zone of the prostate?
items.exp: Benign prostatic hyperplasia originates almost exclusively within the transition zone surrounding the proximal prostatic urethra, directly compressing the urethral lumen.
r: Correct. The transition zone surrounding the urethra is the exclusive site of benign prostatic hyperplasia.
Incorrect. Peripheral zone gives rise to adenocarcinoma.
Incorrect. Central zone surrounds ejaculatory ducts.
Incorrect. External sphincter is striated muscle.
items.kp: Benign prostatic hyperplasia develops within the transition zone of the prostate, leading to bladder outlet obstruction.

items.q: Which parasympathetic spinal cord segments give rise to pelvic splanchnic nerves that stimulate contraction of the detrusor muscle during micturition?
items.exp: Parasympathetic preganglionic neurons arise from the S2-S4 sacral segments (pelvic splanchnic nerves) to stimulate muscarinic M3 receptors on the detrusor, inducing bladder contraction.
r: Correct. S2, S3, and S4 provide parasympathetic motor supply to the detrusor muscle.
Incorrect. T10-T12 mediate sympathetic vasoconstriction.
Incorrect. L1-L2 mediate sympathetic internal sphincter closure (hypogastric nerve).
Incorrect. S1 lacks parasympathetic preganglionic outflow.
items.kp: Sacral parasympathetic nerves from S2-S4 stimulate detrusor muscle contraction and internal sphincter relaxation during micturition.

items.q: The smooth triangular mucosal area at the base of the bladder known as the trigone is bounded by which three anatomical openings?
o: Two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice
Two ejaculatory duct orifices and the urethral crest
Bladder dome and bilateral ureteric orifices
items.exp: The bladder trigone is bounded superolaterally by the two ureteric orifices and inferiorly by the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck.
r: Correct. The trigone is bounded by both ureteric openings and the internal urethral orifice.
Incorrect. Ejaculatory ducts empty into the prostatic urethra.
Incorrect. Prostatic utricle is in the urethra.
Incorrect. Bladder dome is the superior muscular wall.
items.kp: The bladder trigone is bounded by the paired ureteric orifices and the single internal urethral orifice.

items.q: Testicular cancer metastasizes primarily to which regional lymph node group due to the embryological retroperitoneal descent of the testes?
items.exp: Because the testes develop high in the posterior abdominal wall and descend into the scrotum, testicular lymphatic drainage follows the testicular vessels directly to the para-aortic (lumbar) nodes.
r: Correct. Testicular lymphatic drainage travels directly to para-aortic lymph nodes.
Incorrect. Superficial inguinal nodes drain scrotal skin.
Incorrect. Deep inguinal nodes drain lower extremity deep tissues.
Incorrect. Internal iliac nodes drain pelvic viscera including prostate.
items.kp: Testicular lymphatic drainage travels directly to para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes, whereas scrotal skin drains to superficial inguinal nodes.

items.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with sudden severe testicular pain, scrotal swelling, and an absent cremasteric reflex on the affected side. Testicular torsion is confirmed. Which anatomical investment anomaly predisposes to this condition?
o: Bell-clapper deformity (high insertion of tunica vaginalis)
items.exp: The bell-clapper deformity occurs when the tunica vaginalis abnormally envelops the epididymis and spermatic cord, allowing the testis to twist freely on its neurovascular pedicle.
r: Correct. Bell-clapper deformity allows the testis to rotate freely on its pedicle within the tunica vaginalis.
Incorrect. Patent processus vaginalis predisposes to indirect inguinal hernia or hydrocele.
Incorrect. Cryptorchidism increases malignancy risk but bell-clapper is the primary cause of intravaginal torsion.
Incorrect. Tunica albuginea is the dense capsule of the testis itself.
items.kp: Bell-clapper deformity (high attachment of tunica vaginalis) permits free axial rotation, predisposing to testicular torsion.

items.q: What is the dense fibrous connective tissue capsule directly enclosing the testicular parenchyma beneath the visceral layer of the tunica vaginalis?
items.exp: The tunica albuginea is a tough, dense white fibrous capsule that covers the testis and projects inward septa dividing it into testicular lobules.
r: Correct. Tunica albuginea is the fibrous capsule of the testis.
Incorrect. Tunica dartos is smooth muscle in the scrotal wall.
Incorrect. External spermatic fascia is derived from external oblique aponeurosis.
Incorrect. Cremasteric fascia is derived from internal oblique.
items.kp: The tunica albuginea is the dense fibrous capsule enclosing the testicular seminiferous tubules.

items.q: The ejaculatory ducts are formed by the union of the ductus deferens with the excretory duct of which accessory reproductive gland?
items.exp: The ampulla of the ductus deferens joins the excretory duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which courses through the prostate to empty into the prostatic urethra.
r: Correct. Ductus deferens joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct.
Incorrect. Bulbourethral glands empty into the bulbous urethra.
Incorrect. Prostate secretes directly through multiple prostatic ducts.
Incorrect. Littre glands are tiny intraurethral glands.
items.kp: The ejaculatory duct is formed by the union of the ductus deferens and the duct of the seminal vesicle.

items.q: The pampiniform venous plexus surrounding the testicular artery in the spermatic cord cools arterial blood entering the testis. The left testicular vein empties directly into which vessel at a sharp 90-degree angle?
items.exp: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a perpendicular right angle, predisposing to elevated hydrostatic pressure and left-sided varicoceles.
r: Correct. The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a 90-degree angle.
Incorrect. The right testicular vein empties directly into the IVC at an oblique angle.
Incorrect. Internal iliac receives pelvic venous tributaries.
Incorrect. Splenic vein drains portal territory.
items.kp: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein at a 90-degree angle, predisposing to left-sided varicocele.
